page: Amazon Web Services m8idn.32xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance managed by the Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel processors operating at 3.9 GHz, delivering 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled at 2 threads per core. System memory totals 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not include discrete GPU acceleration.

Integrated storage consists of 7600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage, enabling low-latency scratch space and high input/output processing directly on the host. In terms of network performance, the instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps, supporting heavy inter-node traffic and large-scale data transfers. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

The instance delivers high compute density paired with substantial local storage and elevated network bandwidth. Because the bundled 7600 GB NVMe storage is ephemeral instance storage, workloads requiring persistent retention must manage replication across instances or leverage external block storage. The hardware profile is suited for distributed relational and non-relational databases, large-scale caching tiers, search clusters, ETL processing pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idn.32xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel processor running at 3.9 GHz. It features 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs with dedicated CPU allocation, accompanied by 512.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is addressed through 7600 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD instance storage for high-throughput, low-latency I/O operations. The server also incorporates a 200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile, facilitating massive data transfer rates across distributed systems. With no discrete GPUs included, m8idn.32xlarge delivers dense compute, extensive local caching capacity, and high network throughput. These characteristics make it suitable for high-performance databases, large in-memory caches requiring local scratch persistence, real-time telemetry processing, and distributed microservice workloads.
